title: Billings or Sheridan
what_we_know: A 1951 Martinez News-Gazette item (plate 8) calls Angie "owner of the Ideal hotel" while her parents visited her in Billings. Sheridan's Ideal is documented with her from 1955 (plates 14, 15).
what_we_dont: Which Ideal the 1951 item meant. No record places her in control of either hotel in 1951.
what_might_answer_it: Billings and Sheridan city directories for 1950 to 1952; property and license records; hotel advertisements.
evidence_needed: A record naming her with the Billings Ideal, or with Sheridan's before 1955.

title: For Pearl Logan, or with her
what_we_know: The post says she began in Sheridan in some relation to the madam Pearl Logan. The museum holds no record that names Pearl Logan.
what_we_dont: Whether Angie worked for her or with her.
what_might_answer_it: Sheridan license, tax and court records from 1953 on that name both women.
evidence_needed: Any record naming Pearl Logan with Angie or the Rex Hotel.

title: Who told of serving papers at the hotel?
what_we_know: The post says "City Marshal Jack Wolfe described an attempt to serve legal papers at the hotel." The April 2, 1957 clipping (plate 21) gives that account to Sheriff Willard Marshall, and names Jack Wolfe as a local attorney speaking for the hotel. No record names a City Marshal Jack Wolfe.
what_we_dont: Whether any other record of the April 1, 1957 meeting reads otherwise.
what_might_answer_it: The council's own minutes of the April 1, 1957 meeting; the 1957 Sheridan city directory's listing for city marshal.
evidence_needed: The minutes. The clipping already points to an answer; closing it is the curator's call.

title: 171 or 173 North Main
what_we_know: Plate 13's caption gives 171 North Main Street. The post's text, the 1957 incorporation notice (plate 18) and the 1958 revocation (plate 24) give 173.
what_we_dont: Whether 171 is a slip, another number for the same building, or a second address.
what_might_answer_it: Sanborn fire-insurance maps of Sheridan; city directories; county property records.
evidence_needed: A map or property record giving the building's number or numbers.

title: Dyer, Dryer or Dreyer
what_we_know: Jack Alexander's obituary (plate 37) spells her Donna Dreyer. The post's body calls her Donna Dyer, "a woman mentioned in John 'Jack' Alexander's obituary"; its thanks spells Donna Dryer.
what_we_dont: Whether the thanks' Donna Dryer is the same person, and how she spells her name.
evidence_needed: The author's confirmation of the name and spelling.

title: Elko or Sheridan
what_we_know: The post dates the wedding to August 28, 1958 and says it is "strongly believed" to have been in Elko, Nevada. Jack Alexander's obituary (plate 37) says he married Angelina Calicura in 1958 at Sheridan, Wyoming.
what_we_dont: Where they married. The museum holds no marriage record.
what_might_answer_it: Marriage records for 1958 in Elko County, Nevada and Sheridan County, Wyoming.

title: 1960 or the mid 1960s
what_we_know: Jack Alexander's obituary (plate 37) says they moved to South Lake Tahoe in the winter of 1960. The post says the mid 1960s, and records her in Billings through 1965 (plate 29; the Billings Times, as cited). Her own South Lake Tahoe obituary (1986) calls her a 22-year resident: since about 1964.
what_we_dont: When they moved, and whether they moved in stages.
what_might_answer_it: South Lake Tahoe directories of the 1960s; El Dorado County property records; Sierra Pacific Power employment records for Jack Alexander.
evidence_needed: A dated record placing either of them in South Lake Tahoe before 1965.

title: Tarantino's first, or last
what_we_know: The post puts Tarantino's in the 1970s, managed and then bought, before the Tahoe Inn and the Timber Cove. The obituary (plate 37) puts the purchase after she retired from managing the Tahoe Inn and Timber Cove. A 1972 press print (plate 31) has the couple in "their new restaurant," unnamed. Her Martinez obituary (1986) also puts Tarantino's last: Timber Cove was "the latter" of the dining rooms she managed, and "prior to her illness, she operated Angie's Tarentino's."
what_we_dont: The order, and which restaurant the 1972 print means.
what_might_answer_it: Business licenses and directories for South Lake Tahoe, 1970 to 1986; the obituary the post cites for Joe Tarantino's.
evidence_needed: A dated record of the Alexanders' purchase of Tarantino's.

title: Nephew, or a generation further
what_we_know: Plates 12 and 39's captions call Andrew Calicura Angie's nephew. Plates 1 and 2's captions call him her parents' great-grandson, which would make him her great-nephew.
evidence_needed: The family's word on how Andrew is related to Angie.
